title: Somewhere in the east: early morning: set off at dawn. Travel round in front of the sun, steal a day’s march on him. Keep it up for ever never grow a day older technically.
html_source:
If one sets off from Troy, and attempts to outpace the sun, one must be travelling west, as Ulysses would have initially been on his journey home to Ithaca. We know, of course, that after the big storm that pushed them well off course to the Land of the Lotus Eaters, Ulysses and his men were well to the west of Ithaca. Events then pushed them farther northwest until they arrived at the Land of the Dead (quite possibly Monaco), some 1,100 miles west of home: a great distance even by today’s car and ferry.

Monaco

From there, staying ahead of the sun on his way home wouldn’t make sense – unless the appearance on its headpiece of the sun rising from the northwest behind the Bank of Ireland in the risible attempt at nationalism by the newspaper for which Bloom sold advertising, the Freeman Leader, weren’t astronomically absurd.

In that case, if one were passing, say Thrinacia, home of sun god/cattleman Helios, and had been warned by goddess of magic, Circe, as well as the spirit of blind prophet, Tiresius, to avoid the place, one’s judgment and strength of character might be called into question if he were persuaded to stop there by the nagging of his subordinates, as long as they promised not to bother the cattle. If he hadn’t stopped, and had stayed ahead of the sun, not only would Ulysses have gained a day on the sun, and “never [have grown] a day older technically,” he presumably would have returned to Ithaca seven years younger than he was when he eventually did arrive.

anchor.prefix: quietly often as he walked in happy warmth. Boland's breadvan delivering with trays our daily but she prefers yesterday's loaves turnovers crisp crowns hot. Makes you feel young.
anchor.suffix: Walk along a strand, strange land, come to a city gate, sentry there, old ranker too, old Tweedy's big moustaches, leaning on a long kind of a spear. Wander through awned streets.
